text_fidelity_a:
PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV After countless times of the ps4 controllers dying on me due to short battery life, media use on the ps4 was beginning to be a bit of an annoyance. Thankfully, the PDP universal ps4 remote has come to the rescue; well, for the most part. First and foremost, let me say that for the price, it does everything it needs to do and does it well. All of the buttons feel solid and are easy to use, the construction is good, the back is nice and grippy, it is lightweight and because it is a universal remote, it also works on your TV and other electronics. When attempting to use it with my TV it quickly synced itself without issue however I should note I have a Sony television.
If you are looking for a basic remote for Blu-ray movies and Netflix, this is it. It completely solved the battery issue I had with the ps4 remotes, as it has not died on me once. If you are a Hulu user however, you can stop reading, it simply isn’t good enough for Hulu as it can behave somewhat erratically and will not go out of Hulu menus once in them. Outside of Hulu however I have not had a problem with the controller and it functions great with anything else I may need.
There are some minor issues with the remote, for example in order to change the volume you have to switch to the TV controls and then switch back to the ps4 to work with that. It may have just been my controller, and it was easily worked around (use both controllers) but some may find that an issue. When price is factored in, I would say that for the most part, the small annoyances are just that and most users will be able to overlook them. If I had to give a star rating it would be a 4 out of 5 star product. Half a star off for lack of Hulu compatibility and another half off for the little kinks it still has, overall a good product.
text_fidelity_b: PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive Fit (MUF-128BB/AM) I bought 2 of these, they came today, and I and am returning them both tomorrow.

Chief reason: the drive is so small, that it is hard to plug into either USB port in the back of my new TV, a Sony XBR 850C. That TV has a somewhat constricted space where all of its ports are (USB, HDMI, etc). I just learned the hard way that I really need a longer drive to easily insert/remove it with this TV. Anyone else in a similar situation should likewise give this drive a serious rethink. I note that I had little problem with inserting/removing this drive from the front of my workstation, where I have unrestricted space.

Secondary reason: this drive has poor write speeds. My first transfer was of a single 2 GB movie file--a pure sequential write, which should be optimal--and yet I got an initial speed that started at ~50 MB/s and then it decay to maybe 40 MB/s. I should have paid more careful attention to the write benchmarks of this drive. I really want >= 100 MB/s write speeds.

It looks like my best bet is this drive's bigger brother, the Samsung 32GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive MUF-32BA/AM. Ordering 2 right now, stay tuned...
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive Fit (MUF-128BB/AM)

text_fidelity_a: SanDisk 256GB Ultra Dual Drive USB Type-C - USB-C, USB 3.1 - SDDDC2-256G-G46 I bought this to back up my LG phone because I was forced to buy a new phone since LG no longer supports their phones and I was already starting to have issues with mine.  In buying a new phone, I was particularly freaked out about the possibility of losing my photos and other important files since the newer phones no longer have MicroSD cards for backup.  This seemed like a great option--along with backing up to Google and Amazon cloud services, it added another layer of protection.  The problem is that the C port didn't even fit into the C port on my phone--even though I took the case off my phone.  After essentially having to cram it in the port, I kept getting a warning that my data would be corrupted if I kept "ejecting" it.  It also wanted to back everything up to a MicroSD card, since it did not recognize that the SanDisk was even inserted into the phone.  Since I'd spent a considerable amount of time moving everything from my SD card to the internal memory of my phone in anticipation of having to transfer it to a new phone without a card slot, I most definitely didn't want to back up everything back onto my card, so I took the card out.  Even so, it still took quite some time for the phone to recognize the SanDisk, and finally start the back up.  From there, the process was fairly easy, BUT it should have never been so difficult to get the phone to recognize the SanDisk in the first place.  After the backup, I of course plugged the SanDisk into my laptop (without issues) and everything was indeed backed up.  It should NOT have been that difficult to plug the device into my phone however!  I will also mention, not that it's a big deal, but the device is considerably smaller than it looks to be on the Amazon website (less than .75x1.5").  At least I have an additional backup, but not as easily as I would have liked.  Given the issues I had with it I don't think I would purchase this particular device again.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk 256GB Ultra Dual Drive USB Type-C - USB-C, USB 3.1 - SDDDC2-256G-G46

text_fidelity_a:
UltraPro 8K HDMI 2.1 Cable, 6ft. High Speed 48Gbps, 8K @ 60Hz, 4K 1440p 1080p @ 120Hz, HDR VRR eARC QMS, Compatible with PS5 Xbox Series X Roku TV, Streaming, TV, Monitor, All HDMI Devices, 57347 Note: the 4K term is marketing, just about all consumer devices are UHD (2160p). So I'm going to use the UHD term, feel free to translate to "format commonly referred to as 4K" if you prefer.

I tested this cable on my newest UHD tv, with streaming UHD video from multiple sources, and then with a UHD nature documentary on a bluray player. I'd been using a very good 18Gb ("4K") cable before, so possibly a side-by-side test wouldn't show any difference. But I did immediately notice how sharp and bright the picture was in both cases, so I can at least say that this makes a very good video cable for UHD.

The cable is well made and feels sturdy, with a nice grab handle at each end, and inserts just the way it should into HDMI ports, with neither wiggle nor overmuch tightness. I didn't notice any minor flaws that might make me concerned about build quality, and I would expect it to last, at least until it becomes obsolete.

What should you buy if you don't have any so-called 8K media or devices, like most of us, and don't see them in your immediate future? In that case I'd just go with very good "4K" or "8K" cables, but without paying premium prices. The product description might say "Premium High Speed HDMI Cable" (18Gbps) or "Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable" (48Gbps). The first corresponds to the HDMI 2.0b standard, the second to HDMI 2.1.
text_fidelity_b: UltraPro 8K HDMI 2.1 Cable, 6ft. High Speed 48Gbps, 8K @ 60Hz, 4K 1440p 1080p @ 120Hz, HDR VRR eARC QMS, Compatible with PS5 Xbox Series X Roku TV, Streaming, TV, Monitor, All HDMI Devices, 57347

WD has gone to a lot of effort to make this drive world class.

Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version) I have had these for a day. They are absolutely amazing. Life changing, worth every penny. I have seen a lot of reviews where they were compared to AirPods Pros, but there is no comparison.

I bought them because I have a noisy (but lovable) neighbor. The noise cancellation on these is superior, but not for low, bassy, external sounds, but rather sounds in the higher range.

My advise, and to save you some time: Do not get the app. It is so invasive of your information, and I know all apps are, but this one is probably the worst. You can set up bluetooth with all your devices without the app, and use all the features, no problem.

It also has Alexa built in, which is insane, I have yet to pull the trigger on giving Alexa permission, but I think I will; there is an Alexa button, I THINK that's the only time it's listening. If you're like me, and you have Amazon Prime Music the combo is insane.

A few cons: the Noise Cancellation will pound your ears if you’re not listening to content. I didn’t know it could do this, but I can see why people say they can only wear them for so long.

Do not under any circumstance get the app. It’s much more invasive than any app I’ve seen (of tkunborher to read the privacy (publicity) statement. Your earphones can operate fine without the app.

text_fidelity_a: Pard Young Men Smart Watch, Cool Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate Blood Pressure SpO2 Monitor, White The Pard Health Sport Watch has a pedometer (steps taken, distance and calories burned), heart rate monitor (beats per minute), O2 monitor (amount of oxygen in your blood), weather (current temp, high and low temp), messages (must be synced with your smart phone), stopwatch, find feature (locates your phone, in app on phone will locate watch), a blood pressure monitor and an exercise monitor.  The exercise monitor tracks running, cycling, jump roping, table tennis, badminton, tennis and swimming.  The watch is comfortable to wear and looks nice, it has five different watch faces you can choose as your display. I chose this watch because of the blood pressure (bp) monitor, I have high blood pressure and I take medication to keep it normal.  I own two electronic high blood pressure test cuffs and I tested my blood pressure with both of them and the watch and the two cuffs were +/- a point or two apart, but the watch was reading a lot higher than the other monitors.  Throughout the day I repeated the test and the watch was constantly reading that my blood pressure was high, even after I had taken my medication and I know the readings should have changed.  I will have to get with my doctor/nurse and have them do a manual test and see if the watch is showing the same results.  If the watch bp monitor is not accurate, I have not been able to find any way to recalibrate the watch to input the correct bp reading.  That is the only problem I have with this watch.  I like all the features the watch has along with the phone app too.  It doesn't take long to learn all the functions of the watch as well as the app.  If you have high blood pressure, I wouldn't rely on just the watch to monitor your blood pressure because I don't believe it is accurate enough.  Maybe in time there will be an upgrade in the software to fix that. Other than that it is a great sport watch and I am happy with it overall.
text_fidelity_b: Pard Young Men Smart Watch, Cool Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate Blood Pressure SpO2 Monitor, White

Kindle Voyage E-reader, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Adaptive Built-in Light, PagePress Sensors, Wi-Fi It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is.

I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G.

First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. For regular reading, I don't see any reason to switch from a PW2 to a Voyage, but I'd imagine that with illustrations and such, it would make a really big difference. I can actually read at one size smaller font than I could on the PW2.

The light: Nice light, no weird shadings. My device is smoothly lit from bottom to top.

Size/Weight: It's smaller, definitely (not the screen though). Couldn't really see any difference in weight between this and the PW2, but honestly, what's an ounce either way, especially once you start sticking covers on it? It's not something I particularly care about.

Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery.

Wishes/Dreams for the next e-reader: That they'd include text to voice. I doubt this will happen, but I wish it would.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Voyage E-reader, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Adaptive Built-in Light, PagePress Sensors, Wi-Fi

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Z623 400 Watt Home Speaker System, 2.1 Speaker System - Black Latest edit after some frustrating months of use.

I ordered this as a TV speaker. That was in the description.
With no remote, and no way to raise or lower the sound without getting up, the item is useless to me. I like to watch TV in bed.
Who wants to keep getting up. As a computer speaker, it takes up a lot of space.very dissapointed.
I will donate it a church, where they will appreciate a loud speaker for youth groups.

Edit after 5 days use.

There is no remote. The volume is controlled by a dial. When using this connected to your TV, it's a major disadvantage getting up every time you need to change the volume. I have to downgrade from 5 stars to 4, because of this. They need to add to either a remote, or an app letting your phone control the volume. Not a problem when using this as a computer speaker, since the control is by your hand, not across the room. This is promoted as a TV speaker, not just a computer speaker, so it's a major fault.

Original review below.

I have been using the Logitech Z2300 that I purchased years ago. Connected to my computer and much appreciated when I listen to my apple subscription music. A real monster for a computer speaker. Thankfully, the Z 625 is decidedly smaller and fits on the bottom shelf of my 42 inch wood TV table with room to spare. There is also room left for my Amazon Echo and Braven wireless bluetooth speakers. The smaller size results in a much cleaner, more attractive package.

The dialog is much clearer than I expected. I have a ZVOX 450 on my main TV, so I do appreciate clear dialog.
I was disappointed that there is no bluetooth. The computer and Man Cave TV are on opposite sides of the same room, and having the Z2300 for music, and the Z625 for the TV is a bit too much. However, the problem was easily solved. On the Z625, I'm using the optical cable for the TV sound, and am using the enclosed jack to connect the speaker to my extra Iphone. As I type, I'm listening to Herman's Hermits through my Iphone to Z625 jack connection. The music is very soothing and suits my needs perfectly. No adjustments are needed when switching from the music through my smartphone via jack, or the TV sound through the optical cable. Automatic switching,

My TV test via optical was the opening of Game of Thrones. The subwoofer bass sounded great and added greatly to the enjoyment of watching the series. The galloping horses sounded thunderous.

Other considerations. I gave away my monstrous Polk system when we moved to our condo. Soundbars provide the cleanest look but really don't have any bass. My wife is picky. The soundbar is on the main TV for a cleaner appearance, while the Man Cave is a perfect home for this unit.

There was absolutely no documentation/instructions in the box, other than safety information. However hookup instructions were printed on the cardboard box. Don't destroy them opening it. Hooking up via optical was very intuitive and took minutes. I'd still like some instructions. For example, the power button is a push button. Does it shut off after inactivity? I'm doing it manually. Going by the Z2300, it probably won't make any difference. These are built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Z623 400 Watt Home Speaker System, 2.1 Speaker System - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Skullcandy Hesh ANC Wireless Over-Ear Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 22 Hour Battery Life / Best for Music, School, Workouts, Travel, and Gaming - White I have worked with numerous pairs of active noise canceling (ANC phones) and I’ve seen a wide variation in sound profiles, features, and the quality of the ANC function. Some are better than others. I was a bit skeptical of these because of the price; most of the ANC phones I have used that were worth anything have a higher price tag. These are better than the price suggests.

Right out of the box, these headphones do not draw much attention to themselves. They’re not flashy and do not have any noticeable markings on them unless you’re looking for them. They are over-the-ear headphones which tend to be more comfortable than on-ear phones, and these have a snug fit without clamping down tightly. They adjust easily to fit almost any size head too. The padding on the cans is soft enough to not pinch, though after extended wear they do start to get a little warm.

Pairing and connection with my computer was a painless affair and these were ready very quickly after they were powered on.

The ANC function is far and away better than any other headphones I have worked with in this price range. They’re almost as aggressive as that of the Bose QC-15’s that I own, without that weird faux pressure sensation when the ANC is turned on. Even with the volume down low, these cancel out enough background noise to make them a serious contender. I have no complaints with the ANC.

The sound quality is very good, though not quite to my tastes. The bass is very strong – much stronger than I like personally, but not out of line with what has been trending in the last decade. Where Skullcandy got it right, though, is in how well they’ve implemented the bass enhancement. Even though the bass is very strong (enough to give me a headache at higher volumes), it does not distort or turn into just low-frequency noise. More importantly, the bass enhancement does not stomp on the midrange which is the usual casualty. The midrange is warm and fairly balanced. The highs are bright and clear without being piercing. The end result is a sound profile that sounds full and rich. So many headphones with enhanced bass I have used have killed the midrange which makes music sound hollow, or distort the bass so much as to make music sound like a low-fidelity render. These are refreshing in that regard.

Some headphones detect when you take them off and pause music or playback when you take them off. These do not.

These come in a carry pouch that offers little in the way of drop and crush protection but it does keep them clean and free of scuffs and scratches. Also included is an audio cable for wired use as well as a USB Type C cable for charging.

Overall, these are far and away better than the price would suggest. They are very comfortable to wear, they have a good sound profile (particularly if you like heavy bass) and the ANC function is better than average and competitive with much more expensive headphones. These are budget-friendly ANC headphones with higher-end performance.
text_fidelity_b: Skullcandy Hesh ANC Wireless Over-Ear Noise Cancelling Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 22 Hour Battery Life / Best for Music, School, Workouts, Travel, and Gaming - White

text_fidelity_a: Fire TV Stick streaming device with Alexa built in, includes Alexa Voice Remote, HD, latest release I got the newest 4K streaming stick with alexa voice control remote. As of yet i haven't purchased a 4K T.V. but the firestick works on any high def T.V. with a hdmi port. There are lots of free movie and T.V. apps so you can cut the cord and save lots of $$ doing away with cable. You will just have to simply connect a OTA antenna to the back of your TV to receive your local channels. The remote is ok but not great. It does sync easily with your T.V.s CEC control and lets you use the remote for T.V. power on and off. Volume control and alexa voice command. But personally i found it just as quick and easy to manually navigate the apps you want to watch rather than using the button on the remote to ask for a certain app. More times than not the voice control will get what your asking it wrong. But the volume control and power control on the remote is a very good plus over the basic remote. The battery compartment for remote is a little tricky to get opened at first but if you just apply a slight pressure at the same time as sliding the compartment down jt will slide right open. And getting to the streaming quality it will depend on which app you are using. Surprising to me is that the Amazon Prime Video app uses a lot more wifi data than most of the other apps making the shows and movies buffer quite a bit sometimes. I am curious why Amazon Prime uses so much more data vs Netflix or Hulu for example but it surely does. And if you have a Roku device and are used to the Rokus functions it will take a bit of getting used to how the Firestick apps are downloaded and stored compared to the Roku. But they both have equally good and bad comparisons when it comes to their individual functions. Both have excellent picture and sound. What i would really like is for Amazon's firestick to have a remote control app for your android or ios phone. Roku does have the free remote app to download and works great navigating and also has alexa voice control and tou can plug earphones into your phone for private listening. And also remember when buying a firestick to check the gift box if it is going to be used by someone else in their home. If you check the connect to my account box instead all of your information on your other firesticks will be on the new one and also the Amazon buying app with your personal information. So be vigilante and at least have a PIN set up on your Amazon account so no non approved purchases can be made.
text_fidelity_b: Fire TV Stick streaming device with Alexa built in, includes Alexa Voice Remote, HD, latest release

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Rechargeable Touchpad T650 with Windows 8 Multi-Touch Navigation - Black I am loving the Logitech Rechargeable Touchpad T650 with its user-friendly ease of use and many great features. The small size of 5 1/4" width x 5" length, smooth surface, rechargeable battery, very responsive with light-touch to activate gestures, on/off switch, place anywhere to use and sturdy design makes this the perfect touchpad for me. I got this touchpad as my computer mouse stopped working. I thought about a touchscreen monitor, but opted for this touchpad instead as it would be so nice to not have to stretch and fatigue my arm with the actions needed with a touchscreen monitor. The touchpad only needs a very light touch of the fingers to click, slide and navigate the gestures to activate the product features, which is most excellent to keep stress off the fingers. I have a desktop computer with Windows 7 right now, but this touchpad supports Windows 8 when I make the change which is another plus for me. Note a gesture not listed on the Logitech site that I just happen to notice worked to activate the right mouse click is a very light tap of two fingers in the middle of the touchpad. Also, note that a two-handed gesture not listed on the Logitech site that I found useful to highlight is to apply pressure to the left-hand bottom corner of the touchpad with the other hand lightly touch the touchpad with a smooth move of the cursor to highlight, then release the pressure on the touchpad to end highlighting-- after you have finished with copy and paste or drag and drop, to release the highlighted text--place the cursor on the highlighted area then lightly tap anywhere on the touchpad with one finger. Make sure to download the latest version of software for this touchpad to avoid possible glitches. It took me less than a day to get used to using this touchpad, and I find this touchpad superior to a mouse. I highly recommend this rechargeable touchpad and hope this review is helpful to others.

Tips for this touchpad's gestures (includes some that I wrote above):

(1.) To activate the right mouse click is a very light tap of two fingers in the middle of the touchpad.

(2.) A two-handed gesture to highlight is to apply pressure to the left-hand bottom corner of the touchpad and with the other hand lightly touch the touchpad with a smooth move of the cursor to highlight, then release the pressure on the touchpad to end highlighting-- after you have finished with copy and paste or drag and drop, to release the highlighted text--place the cursor on the highlighted area then lightly tap anywhere on the touchpad with one finger.

(3.) Download the latest version of software for this touchpad to avoid possible glitches.

(4.) Use the on/off switch on the top right side of touchpad to turn off when not in use for a long period of time to save the rechargeable battery.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Rechargeable Touchpad T650 with Windows 8 Multi-Touch Navigation - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola SH001 VerveOnes Completely Wireless Smart Earbuds This is a great idea that has been done by many companies. I would have hoped that motorola would have been able to nail down the design and build of these earbuds to work well. Maybe this is the first batch that came out and its just being buggy with the firmware but there are some things that are frustrating with this headset especially when they have some out for less then $100.

As others have stated, when you have the earbuds in, they both are required to be in or the music stops playing. At first this seems like a good idea but when you want to listen to whats going on around you, you'll also be pausing music.

They feel a little awkward in the ear, doesn't feel very secure if running around, but in the gym they seemed to work well enough unless jumping around.

I understand why the earbuds need to be connected to the dock to change settings but they are bluetooth. It should be a simple enough solution to change all the settings in the app or device being used without having to put them in the dock every time.

Battery life has not been great with the advertised 12 hours. Usually getting a few hours out of them and thats with using them when i first got them letting them die all the way and then charging them up.

I along with a handful of others appear to be having issues with the right earbud dropping out randomly... kinda odd, might be a firmware thing but unknown.

For the money, I would wait till Motorola is able to make a second pass over this product. Update the firmware and figure out if the glitches are hardware based or in the firmware.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola SH001 VerveOnes Completely Wireless Smart Earbuds

I tried it with both my 2017 15" Intel MB Pro and the redesigned 2020 16" MB Pro with a thicker bottom case.

I tend to lean my hands on the edge of my laptop, so I found the rise on the edge to be somewhat high when using it with my older computer, although I do appreciate having the extra fans for cooling on that model because Intel Mac Books Pro models tend to overheat.

This stand can handle the weight of both machines, with the latter coming in at over 4lbs, along with the weight of my hands leaning on it, and there was no indication of it wanting to sag or sink in any way. It will stay put at whatever angle or height you choose. At least it did for me.

I like having a slight angle when I type, and being able to raise my screen's camera to eye level so I am not looking down at it during Zoom meetings for that double chin effect. It's also convenient to have that little nook of space to tuck any cables and SSDs underneath, and out of the way.

There is about an inch to two inches of overhang on either side with larger computers, but it's not much, and both computers felt stable.

Overall, I would say it's a very good, and high-quality laptop stand. However, it is a bit smaller than I expected.

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized These headphones are the most comfortable I have ever owned. The ear cups sit flat against the ear, which feels more natural than the usual headphone with ear cups that surround your ear with a hot and sweaty dome. I could only handle that style for a while and then my ears needed a cool off to dry out. If you are using these headphones somewhere loud, like a train stop, the environment noises will interfere a bit, same if you turn the volume up bystanders will hear it. But the lack of hot and sweaty ears is such a bonus so these other problems are easily avoided.

The headphones are instantly compatible with all smartphones with a headphone jack. I used it on a Google Pixel and on iPhone 5's the sound quality was crystal clear, much better than any bluetooth headset I've ever had, and I've had plenty.

The USB adapter with the call controls worked great for my business calls GoToMeeting, Skype for Business and Google Voice.

The cord is three feet long, perfect for me since I get tired of getting the cord tangled as I pace around during calls, but it might be a bit on the short side for some. For use with the computer the USB adds two feet between the USB port and the controlling buttons. The cord is round, and so far, has been resistant to kinks.

The volume and mute buttons are on the cord instead of the headset, I like this because I don't have to memorize the placement during a call and the indicator light for mute keeps me from forgetting that I have muted a call and no one can hear me because I muted to sneeze, cough or shush my cat.

The only drawback is that unlike with a bluetooth headset there are no volume or mute controls as part of the headset or cord when it is plugged into a smart phone.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized

Unfortunately, no one where she lived knew how to set it up and she died before we could set it up for her. So I basically wasted $145 for two Echo Shows because the one we have at home is no prize.)

(I have upgraded my review to take off a star. Since we have not been able to do face-to-face calling on it--no one where my MIL lives knows how to set it up--it basically is useless for the purpose we got it. Yeah, I loaded some photos on it so now I can look up and see our previous dog or a pic of my mom. But really, the old 2nd Generation Echo Dot responded better and more quickly. THIS THING IS DEAF. I used to be able to call up the stairs before I took the dog out "Echo, what's the temperature outside?" and like THAT I'd get a response. You have to bellow at the Show two or three times. Sometimes I have to stand right next to it to make it listen. But it loves my husband's voice and always responds. The drop-ins were crisp and clear on the Dot. It was a real waste of money.)

We had a bright idea: buy one of these for us, and buy one for my husband's mother, so we could video call her at any time (she lives 2 hours drive away), and his sister who lives in with his mom. Right now we are not making much use of the screen, save for a clock and a thermometer, but we have branched out into routines that are rather fun. We have tried out its video capabilities and that is very good, although we have trouble with backlighting from where our Show is placed.

I have two complaints about the Show: I think the voice is more muffled, and it doesn't seem as voice responsive as the Dot. If anything is running in the background, like the television or music, it gets really hard of hearing. We have to shout.

Certain sounds seem to cause more problems than others, including dropped audio, glitchy video, and sometimes a blank screen. This happens with both XBox Ones and a PS3. I mainly play Forza 6 and Gran Turismo 6, and certain engine sounds seem to be associated with these problems more than others. Streaming video doesn't seem to cause any problems with any of the input devices or either TV. The normal solution is to cycle the power off and back on. Different cables or settings don't seem to make a difference. I'm not using the audio splitter at all. Personal opinion (from decades of experience with processors of all kinds), is that whatever processor is used simply cannot process some sounds correctly, even to pass the signal through. I may be wrong. I've been wrong before. This may be a quality control issue, or it may be an engineering issue. Either way, I'm looking for a better product, and most of the ones in this price range seem to be identical except for the name on the box. In fact, many more expensive devices seem to be exactly the same layout, and likely use the same circuitry. There's no way to tell from the name on the box, or the Amazon description.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony BDP-BX370 Blu-ray Disc Player with built-in Wi-Fi and HDMI cable UPDATE 05/15/2021 - It lasted less than two weeks and it died. During playback the player freezes on discs known to be good, and in order to get6 the player to respond I have to disconnect the power from it. It was great while it lasted, I guess.

Original review follows.

===

I have wanted a Blu-Ray player for a while and I have had reason to suspect that my DVD player is dying. I have a flat-screen Sony television so I figured this player would connect and work with it without too much effort. I was right and it has worked very well for my family and me.

This is a straightforward device. I connected it to the TV via the provided HDMI cable, selected that input and immediately was able to get signal from it. I popped in a disc and it loaded up to the menu. That’s exactly what I expected to happen. In operation using the remote it has worked very much like my old DVD player – remote is laid out a bit differently but the operation is the same and it provides buttons to stop, fast forward and reverse, pause, eject, select the root menu and more. The remote had given us no issues so far, though it does need to have near line-of-site with the player in order for the player to see it and respond.

The footprint is much smaller than my older DVD player and required a bit of rearrangement in my entertainment center. The whole unit is smaller than a ream of paper and weighs next to nothing.

It has built-in WiFi and makes it easy to access online streaming services. However, I will confess that I haven’t yet tried this as I try to keep my WiFi device list small. I will experiment with this when there is time.

So far we have seen no issues with playback – no skips or stutters or freezes. I have a couple of discs that I know to cause issues for my DVD player that I will try in this player and see if it fares better, though I believe the discs are actually bad.

So far I have had a positive experience with this player and based on that I am happy to recommend it. It seems to work well and it is easy to understand and operate. It isn’t particularly expensive either which is a big plus.
text_fidelity_b: Sony BDP-BX370 Blu-ray Disc Player with built-in Wi-Fi and HDMI cable

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb Growing up I always had a radio in my room. Times are a little different now and I tend to get my music from the Internet, but there are still times when local radio stations are a better choice - particularly during power outages or when getting local news. I have had very good fortune with Sony electronics and computers in the past so I was eager to try this AM/FM tuner and had high expectations. It did not disappoint me.

Let me very clear about this unit - it is for AM/FM receiving only. It does not play MP3’s, it doesn’t play CDs and it doesn’t stream from the Internet. It’s just an AM/FM tuner. It does this quite well, though - better than most other tuners I have used in the last several years.

Right out of the box, this unit looks nostalgic. It has a classic AM/FM radio look and feel, very similar to a radio my father used to have in his workshop when I was a kid. This is a big plus for me, just for the fact that it takes me back to my childhood.

I plugged it in and turned it on, and I immediately tuned to one of the [relatively] local stations. It picked it up and played it very clearly, better than most other tuners I have used in the last 4-5 years. It is definitely better than the car’s radio. I “surfed” the dial and found other stations that I have listened to in the past but thought were out of range and this little radio did a good job of picking them up and playing with minimal static. That’s really all I could ask. It’s not a miracle radio though and it cannot pick up FM stations hundreds of miles away, but it has better range than most I have used recently.

I like that it can be used on AC power or on batteries. That will be handy during weather events.

I can’t find any real reason to complain about this tuner. It works great and looks great too. It is a little on the pricey side which is par for the course for Sony electronics, but it is a fine tuner that is worth its asking price.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb

text_fidelity_a: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN Buyers should note that this drive is formatted in exFAT. Without knowing this, I plugged it in to a running computer and began to transfer some files. The computer was shut down for the night. The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. I have several Western Digital external drives and this is the first one that arrived in a format other than NTFS.
text_fidelity_b: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN

text_fidelity_a:
Eyefi mobiProZ-32 Mobi Pro 32GB WiFi SDHC CARD with One Year Eyefi Cloud This EYE-FI MOBI PRO 32GB WIFI SDHC CARD replaces my "legacy" [[ASIN:B003DV4234 Eye-Fi Connect X2 Wi-Fi SDHC Card]] (which still works perfectly after 3+ years of regular use). These Eye-Fi SDHC cards are incredibly convenient for a casual photographer like myself. The photos are immediately uploaded to my computer or to the Eye-Fi Cloud, right after they're shot. The photos can be shared immediately, and I don't have to remove the card from my camera to transfer the photos to a PC or mobile device. (The Eye-Fi cards can also be read directly from a photo card reader or from a PC card reader slot.)

This Eye-Fi Mobi Pro card is much, much faster than my "legacy" Eye-Fi card. The Mobi Pro works just like the older card in my Panasonic Lumix DMC-LX2S camera. (The Eye-Fi web site has a long, long list of compatible cameras you can check before buying any Eye-Fi card.)

Uploads to the Eye-Fi Cloud seem almost instantaneous, and the transfers to my PC take about a quarter of the time required by the older card. The wireless transmissions do tend to drain my camera battery though. You'll need to recharge frequently or keep extra batteries on hand.

The Eye-Fi Mobi Pro app transfers your photos and videos directly into "Eye-Fi Pictures", "Eye-Fi RAW", and "Eye-Fi Videos" folders on your PC. The software's default setting groups the transferred files into subfolders of these folders by date.

The Mobi Pro app also uploads your photos to the Eye-Fi Cloud and groups them by date. In the Eye-Fi Cloud you can do simple editing (rotate, crop), add captions, and create albums. You get a one-year free subscription to the Eye-Fi Cloud with each Mobi Pro card; renewals are $4.99 a month, or $49.99 a year. The Eye-Fi Cloud is a convenience, but your Mobi Pro card will continue to be completely functional if you decide that you don't need the Eye-Fi Cloud storage. You can upload to the Eye-Fi Cloud from anywhere, not just from your home network.

You get the Mobi Pro app/software by going to the web address printed on the box (just below the space for the included card reader). The software is clean and simple, with settings for uploading and downloading photos--automatically or manually--to either the Eye-Fi Cloud, your PC, or both.

I always have to fuss for a while to get any Eye-Fi software set up properly. (Tip: Don't try to set up the Eye-Fi Mobi app on two PCs at once, with both PCs turned on. This confuses the software, and also the wireless connections. I had to uninstall the software from one PC, and recycle my router because my PC lost the ability to communicate with the router. The price I paid for stupidity!)

Ever since I got my first Eye-Fi card, I haven't wanted to use anything else in my camera. This Eye-Fi Mobi Pro card is tremendously advanced over that first card, in both speed and versatility, and I love it even more.
text_fidelity_b: Eyefi mobiProZ-32 Mobi Pro 32GB WiFi SDHC CARD with One Year Eyefi Cloud

Amazon Basics microSDXC Memory Card with Full Size Adapter, A2, U3, Read Speed up to 100 MB/s, 64 GB, Pack of 2, Black I selected this memory card because I needed one for a dash cam. When it comes to storage, name bands are usually the way to go when you need something really reliable, so I was a little hesitant at first to use a "store brand" card. So far, it has been fine and I have no complaints, though it will take time and more use to determine if it will hold up long-term.

The card I received is a 128GB MicroSD with an adapter. The adapter makes it work in a camera like my mirrorless, but I would not recommend this kind of set-up unless pressed. The adapter is really most useful when pulling data from the card in a machine that does not have a slot for a MicroSD, so the adapter does have its place.

The card fit in my dash cam with no issues and the cam seems to be happy with it. It detects the presence of the card and the full capacity of it which is good. Being a class 10 card it is fast enough to keep up with the recording and in a 45 minute trip it did not skip or stutter once. Quality seems to be fine. Using the adapter, my PC has no trouble reading the card and reformatting when I want to quickly erase it.

So far, this card has worked out just fine and I am pleased with it. It's priced well and it seems to work well in the way I need it to work. Time will tell if it will hold up, but so far all indicators are positive.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics microSDXC Memory Card with Full Size Adapter, A2, U3, Read Speed up to 100 MB/s, 64 GB, Pack of 2, Black

Verbatim 32GB Store 'n' Flip USB Flash Drive - Violet, 0.3 x 0.8 x 2.2 I have had good fortune with Verbatim products in the past, particularly blank CDs. I was excited to try this thumb drive and it has worked out well for me so far. The biggest plus is the size of the whole unit.

This is a 32GB drive which is a good size for most things anymore. It is good as a mass storage device but it also is suitable as boot media if you need to use it for recovery media, OS replacement or other things. There are bigger thumbs drives out there, but this one is big enough for most.

It comes preformatted with a FAT32 file system which makes it easy to read by practically all modern operating systems. My Linux system is able to mount it and read it, and Windows 10 opens it automatically. I likely will reformat it though for a better-performing file system to use primarily on my Linux system.

I looked on the drive for hidden files and found only the system volume stuff.

I did not make notes on the read/write speeds but it seems to perform on par with other name-brand drives I have. I have worked with drives that are quite slow when copying larger files like ISO images; this one seems about average when compared to Sandisk and PNY drives.

Where this drive really distinguishes itself, though, is in the very small size, which is good but also could be a problem. It folds up to about the size of a nickel (approximately) and easily fits in a change pocket. This keeps it out of the way and makes it easy to toss in a bag, purse, pocket or backpack even when it’s full. However, it also means it can easily find its way into the laundry.

So far, I have no complaints with this drive and am happy to recommend it. It performs well, it is easily recognized on different platforms and is small enough to go just about anywhere.
text_fidelity_b: Verbatim 32GB Store 'n' Flip USB Flash Drive - Violet, 0.3 x 0.8 x 2.2

Lemorele USB C Hub, 10-in-1 USB C Dongle, USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter with HDMI 4K 60Hz, Gigabit Ethernet, 100W Power Delivery, 2 USB 3.0 Ports, SD/TF Card Reader for MacBook Pro/Air Type C Laptops I got this because my laptop has only 3 USB C ports and no standard USB ports. One of them is for power, and I've got a wireless mouse and keyboard, which leaves one port for everything else.
Needless to say, I need a few more ports and also an ethernet connection (RJ45).
The unit comes nicely boxed and for some reason has a bunch of stickers for the flags of various countries. Not sure why, but it's an interesting approach.
It has a lot of ports, an HDMI, RJ45,SD Card and micro SD, 1 USB C, 1 PD, which looks like a USB C, but is a power port, 2 USB 2.0 and 2 USB 3.0.
There is a warning label that says it might get hot (up to 130" F) and thatdevices with power higher than 7.5W are not supported, so check on the things you will be plugging into the hub before you buy it. It also says the PD adapter is under 40W and may not be able to charge all devices through the hub.
So, if you are going to use this to power a bunch of USB devices or charge your phones, it might not work. But if you are just plugging things in like cameras, microphones or drives then it will work fine.
For having all those ports, it's not as large as some others I've used and all in all is a nice hub. If you need more ports, then this is definitely worth considering.

Rii (Newest Version) K12+ Mini Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad Mouse, Stainless Steel Portable Wireless Keyboard with USB Receiver for MacBook/iPad/Tablet/PC/Laptop/Smart TV/Raspberry Pi - Black It helps to have small hands to use this small keyboard, and I almost got used to scrunching my hands together to type with it. Until I needed to enter an underscore. The -_ key should be located to the right of the 0 key. Since high school that's where my right hand is trained to go for that key. But on this keyboard it's two keys right of the space bar. What???? Keyboard manufacturers really need to stop rearranging the keys we've all learned to locate on a standard keyboard layout. I know compromises sometimes need to be made for a small form factor, but this is really a deal-breaker for me, so I'm returning. I also found the touchpad precision to be below average even after tinkering with the Windows mouse settings. Ehhhhh.

UPDATE: I checked the product photos, and in the first two pictures the -_ key is in the expected location, but in the next two pictures the -_ key is in the awkward location as it was in the keyboard I received. Granted, on the box it says "THE MANUFACTURER RESERVES THE RIGHT TO AMEND THE SPECIFICATIONS WITHOUT PRIOR NOTIFICATION. THE PICTURES AND DATE IN THE STYLEBOOK ARE FOR CONSULT ONLY IF THERE IS FLUCTUATION..." (Not sure this is a "right"... sounds more like an "adopted business practice" to eschew product configuration management). Well, I reserve the "right" to return for refund a product that isn't the same as what's in the pictures.

So in other words you might receive the product shown in pics 1-2, or pics 3-4, or something different.

Disclaimer: My negative review starkly contrasts with the glowing 5-star reviews from the many reviewers who received this product free in exchange for a review. However, since I PAID FULL PRICE for this item, my standards may admittedly be somewhat higher.

text_fidelity_a:
Arteck 2.4G Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo Ultra Compact Slim Stainless Full Size Keyboard and Ergonomic Mouse for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop and Windows 10/8/7 Build in Rechargeable Battery ARTECK HW086MW162 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse combo, still charging that's why there are cables. Pen in the photo for size reference, along with the box it came in.

Unboxing was “frustration free” as advertised. I recycled my Logitech cord that connected to my desktop and inserted the USB receiver in it and it worked.

I plugged in the Micro USB charging cable to the keyboard and mouse. Only one Micro USB charging cable came with the combo so I used an extra Android Micro USB charging cable to charge both at the same time.

I was able to use the keyboard and mouse in a few moments. My computer automatically updated the files needed in a few minutes.

All in all the unboxing and set up was quick and effortless. Now I am going to explore the keyboard.

This keyboard has no number side keyboard that makes it smaller.

It has a blue function key to access page up, page down, home, and end, on the lower right where the left, right, up, down keys are.

Along the top with the F keys are blue function commands:

Escape has “Media” – when pressed opened Wave Pad, a NCH program I have installed.

F1 has an >/||, which did nothing when pressed

F2 has |<<, which did nothing when pressed

F3 has >>|, which did nothing when pressed

F4 has a speaker symbol )x, That mutes sound

F5 has a speaker symbol - which lowers volume

F6 has a speaker symbol + which increases volume

F7 has a symbol for home, which opens a new browser tab

F8 has a symbol of a magnifying glass that opens a search side window and uses Bing for search, when I clicked on one of the search results it opened a new Chrome tab. I had Chrome already opened.

F9 has a symbol for a folder, which did nothing when pressed

F10 has a symbol for power which turned off my computer. Since I had programs opened my computer asked for permission so I canceled.

F11 has “insert” on it which is pretty self explanatory

F 12 has “PrtSc” for print screen

The action on the keyboard is nice and a lot quieter than the Logitech keyboard I am replacing. The mouse action is good and also quiet.

For less than $23 this is a good keyboard and mouse. I never used the number keys on the side of my Logitech keyboard, which needed batteries, as did the mouse that came with it. The mouse had begun to do double clicks when I clicked once and the keyboard “enter” would stay down. That's why I replaced them for this Arteck Keyboard and Mouse combo. To be able to stop buying and replacing batteries and the small space it takes up, along with it is quiet, makes my money well spent.
text_fidelity_b: Arteck 2.4G Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo Ultra Compact Slim Stainless Full Size Keyboard and Ergonomic Mouse for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop and Windows 10/8/7 Build in Rechargeable Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray) I debated for a long time about getting a tablet. A couple years ago I'd have sworn that I'd never have one. I've been a laptop guy for a long time and love the PC, but it gets cumbersome some times. You can't do everything with a tablet that you can with a PC, but for most people it can fill most of your needs. Smart phones are nice but they're just to small for my eyes and big fingers. Besides, my view of cell phones is something to make calls with and talk on.

That said as I read and looked at different tablets, I realized the potential for their use. I've got issues with Apple and didn't want to go the ipad route for a number of reasons. I did some research on the new Windows tablets and I like the idea, but they've got a way to go. I think they rushed it to get it to market. I like the ideas behind Android and although a lot of the apps are designed more for smart phones, apps optimized for tablets are increasing and all the other smart phone designed apps work. The open source design makes for all sorts of obscure market apps. Plenty of developers out there. You can find some weird stuff for Android that you won't find on other platforms. Lots of pretty good free apps and plenty of cheap stuff too that is impressive.

So next I had to decide on size. For 99% of my uses, the 10 inch seemed to be the better choice and with a number of these with docking key pads available, I went that way rather than the smaller versions. So then I had to decide which one. It didn't take long to realize that ASUS was probably the leader in the field and known for very high quality products. Likewise it only took a bit longer to see that the Infinity TF700 with 64GB, was the machine to have. I also opted for the docking keypad.

The tablet is very impressive. The screen resolution is right up there with the best ipad. The NVIDIA quad core CPU is a screamer. Can't get much better. Cameras are very good. Battery life is good and amazing with the dock which also has a battery in it. With all the features together, I think this is the best Android tablet out there today and most pro revues agree.

As a new user to this scene, I'm sure others may have different ideas that got me to this choice, but I can say that I am completely satisfied. That said, as a "newbie" I suppose you might think anything would seem that way, however, I did a lot of research and hands on comparisons and I'm comfortable I bought the best.

I am 99.9% thrilled with it. If it has a flaw, it's probably the speaker which faces the wrong way in my opinion and doesn't have quite the volume and sound quality I'd like. It is fine in a quiet environment, but if there's any background noise it leaves a bit to be desired. I have found that if you hold it with your hand somewhat loosely cupped behind the speaker, the sound level improves dramatically as your hand reflects if towrd you. It is fine with ear buds and I also recently picked up a great little bluetooth speaker, (Clalrity HD by Monster), that kicks butt.

Everything else about the Infinity TF700 seems perfect. The only other way to make it better would be built in 4G and phone capability. If I'm mobile I use mine with a Verizon Jet Pack, which is an awesome device itself. Even on 3G it works better than my built in mobile broadband in my laptop.

Do your own research and get some hands on time if you can to compare because all tablets are not equal. There is no doubt that as far as tablets go, a lot has to do with how you will use it and what for. But if you want the best Android tablet in the 10 inch size range, you can't beat the Infinity TF700. This thing is awesome!
text_fidelity_b: Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray)

Portable Photo Studio,URiver Mini LED Light Box Kit Folding Table Top and 4 Backdrops Photography Lighting Tent (Size:9.5" x 9.5" x 8.7") Read the description well and you will see that this is for very small items, which suits me fine since I bought it to photograph jewelry and other tiny things that I make.

First, you HAVE to look at the pictures in the directions in order to set this up and tear it down without damaging it. The snaps on the side are plastic, as are the walls, and it takes a gentle hand to put it together without damaging it. It took me a second to realize that if you force any of the parts of this, something's gonna break. So now, I managed to put it together and discovered the backdrops, and for just that one reason, this got five stars. I have no idea who out there in Amazon-land takes pictures of jewelry or small items, but getting the background to blend or contrast well with the subject is very difficult when you don't have a lot of choices. This comes with backdrops of black, white, green, and red. I took pictures with a couple of the colors because I was so pleased at the way they turned out. I use a tiny tripod and a digital camera to take my pictures, and this is a very good height to work with the small tripod. The pendant drop in the first picture is about 1-1/2" long and photographed wonderfully in this studio. I'm sold, and would definitely buy again, and would recommend it for anyone taking pictures of miniatures of any kind.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Photo Studio,URiver Mini LED Light Box Kit Folding Table Top and 4 Backdrops Photography Lighting Tent (Size:9.5" x 9.5" x 8.7")

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black I will cut to the chase and briefly summarize right off the bat - I have a Targus Legend IQ backpack-style laptop bag that I prefer to this bag. This is not a bad bag at all and I think it suits the need nicely, but I think there are equivalent bags available for less money.

The most important feature of any laptop bag, whether it's a backpack-style bag or an attache case bag, is protection for the laptop it carries. This particular bag does provide reasonable padding, though this padding is a little thin on the bottom which is an area where I think most of the padding is actually needed. I would be very wary of dropping this bag from all but the shortest distances from the ground as there just isn't the kind of cushion needed. This is, in my eyes, the biggest flaw in this bag, though to be fair most backpack-style bags have less padding on the bottom than required so I can't really single this out as making this bag any worse off than any other I have used.

Pockets - storage compartments are important when transporting computer equipment and this bag has a lot of them. Including the divider in the main compartment there are no less than nine compartments in this bag, each of varying utility. I especially appreciate the small zippered compartments on the sides of the bag which are perfect for small flashlights and USB sticks. The main compartment is suitable for a laptop and a tablet or even two smaller laptops. The front zippered compartment, though spacious, gets a little cramped when storing a power cord and a trackball together.

This is a well-constructed bag that appears to be very sturdy and rugged. One weak spot I have seen in several other bags of this type is the top handle strap that has a bad tendency to rip loose. I do not think this is going to be a problem for this bag - the stitching is high quality and the tight-weave nylon should make this bag's handle hold for a long time.

So, what is my main complaint with this bag? It's the price. As I write this, this bag sells for ~$90 full-price. My Targus bag which is roughly equivalent in quality and utility sells for about half that price. When I can get the same usefulness from a product that costs so much less, I have trouble justifying the expense.

The bag itself is a good bag and I think it will serve well for anyone looking for a good, rugged and spacious laptop bag. The price, however, gives me pause when there are less expensive options readily available.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black

Microsoft Wireless Comfort Desktop 5000 Not being a techie, this review will be based on the experiences of an average Joe or Jane trying this keyboard on for size.

Pros:

1. Excellent packaging. Easy to open, and is packed in a compact and attractive box. Would make a great gift.
2. Nice comfortable palm rest and key positioning. The removable feet required a bit of reading of the instructions to set up, but this was relatively easily accomplished. Note: Be careful you don't throw out the feet with the packaging.
3. Easy set up. Up and running in minutes.
4. Works with batteries, so no need to store and locate a charger when the mouse runs out of steam. (As compared to the Logitech model)
5. Handy buttons for MS Office, such as cut, copy, paste, undo, bold, italic and underline (et al) right on the keyboard. (as dual key functions)
6. Media keys and volume controls on keyboard, also low battery indicator light.
7. Compact footprint, so it can fit most workstations.

Cons:

1. Can you say "dust magnet"? This thing picks up dust and fingerprints like crazy, especially on the shiny bits.
2. Lack of detailed instructions for the keyboard and mouse. It comes with adequate set-up instructions, but expects you to know what to do after that. I'd have appreciated some included info on the keyboard functions.
3. No lights for Caps lock and Num lock
4. Mouse has no on/off switch (that I can find), so when I turned it over and put in the batteries (2 x AA included) I nearly blinded myself with the blue laser. Note: It turns off when the receiver is stored in the base.
5. Mouse is obese. Hard for small hands to deal with, and not ergonomic.

Note:
I don't have Windows 7 as yet, but it's nice to know that whenever I get it, the keyboard has special "hot keys" to allow easy access to programmes.

Overall, a good keyboard/mouse combination for the price, with more positive features than negative if you're an average computer user. I can't speak for Gamers or Techies, but I like it.

Amanda Richards, January 3, 2010
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless Comfort Desktop 5000

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114) I travel quite a bit and many of the trips I take are short in duration- often only two or three nights. I don’t need a lot of luggage space for these short trips and I like taking backpacks because I can often avoid carry- on and baggage fees if my backpack can fit under my seat. This desire for economical travel led me to get the Case Logic BRYBPR116 Bryker Backpack Roller.

With this Case Logic Backpack, you get a two-in-one backpack and piece of luggage well suited for travel or business. The wheels make it perfect for traversing an airport and with the added straps, you can carry it on your back, like a traditional backpack. There is an outside pocket where you can tuck the straps so they are not hanging out, flopping around when you don’t need them. And the handle can be completely pushed inside the backpack and sealed off with a zipper so that no one sees it. I like these qualities because it means I can make this look like a backpack when I want it to and I can make it look more like a piece of luggage when I want it to.

Inside the backpack, there is a separate compartment for a laptop and I like that you can unsnap this if you like, making for a larger interior space that is just right for stuffing your two- day supply of clothing and personal items. Like I said, my primary usage with this backpack is for travel and I usually don’t take my laptop with me when I’m on a two- day trip, so I would rather have the open space, to make it more like a piece of luggage.

There is one thing to keep in mind if you take this backpack on a plane, and that is the size of pack makes it only barely able to fit under your seat. It will stick out some, so be prepared to have a snug space where your feet normally go. And unlike other backpacks, it’s too rigid- thanks to the handle- to make it collapsible and flexible. To save having to pay carry- on fees on certain airlines, I am willing to place it under the airline seat in front of me regardless, even if it does stick out some. If your flying on an airline that doesn’t charge extra for carry-ons, then this won’t be an issue since you can easily place the backpack in the overhead, which is what I recommend doing. For everyone else, just bear in mind that the length of the backpack makes it a challenge to fit under a seat.

I have a wide assortment of backpacks and luggage in my home to accommodate different needs. This Case Logic rolling backpack is a nice addition to my collection and I like that it performs a dual role. It has suited me well so far and it makes a good choice of luggage/backpack for business people and others who are constantly on the go for short spans of time.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114)

Logitech MK345 Wireless Combo Full-Sized Keyboard with Palm Rest and Comfortable Right-Handed Mouse, 2.4 GHz Wireless USB Receiver, Compatible with PC, Laptop Updated 6/5/2021
After having problems with the keyboard's wireless signal registering with the PC, I took another reviewer's suggestion and purchased a 6 foot USB extension cord, attached the wireless receiver to it, and mounted it to the top of my large screen display. This resolved the line-of-sight issues and now both the keyboard and the mouse function well.

I would have given 5 stars but...
I have purchased quite a few Logitech wireless keyboards/mouses/combos over the years and have been satisfied. With this purchase, I constantly have problems with the keyboard signals being received by the PC (never a problem with the mouse though!). The PC either does not receive the signal at all, or it takes a quite a few persistent attempts (usually by adjusting line-of-sight) for it to function. Doesn't make sense. If the mouse is completely unaffected, why would the keyboard if they are right next to each other?
Never had this problem with the other Logitech keyboard/mouse combo and it is the same model #.
Granted, I have a large 55" display between my desk and the PC, but still...
Going to try what another reviewer suggested and get a USB extension cable and attach the the receiver to it and tape it the top of the screen.
I definitely like the size and overall performance of this model, that's why I have ordered it twice.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MK345 Wireless Combo Full-Sized Keyboard with Palm Rest and Comfortable Right-Handed Mouse, 2.4 GHz Wireless USB Receiver, Compatible with PC, Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Apptivity Gym for iPhone & iPod Touch Devices My five-month-old daughter loves this thing. Well, so far. We've had it for a couple weeks, and bust it out whenever we're home and she's awake, and we have some free time (which is hardly ever, but still). When I realized the apps uses with this is the same as the [[ASIN:B0080D58GA Fisher-Price bConnect Digital Soother]], I just flipped it over to the mirror and let her play with the toys.

My complaints are that the mirror is embedded behind the clear film (which would prevent the baby from touching the phone), so the reflection is milky. Also, because of her size, the mirror doesn't reach her face when she plays with the toys, so it's kind of useless anyway.

We don't really use the straps on the sides to hang the toys as her little arms won't be able to reach them on either side when she's lying in the middle, so we just hook `em all on the centered rings and she likes them just fine.

It's easily portable, though I question its price-point. It's worth $20, in my opinion. Also, if you have newer iPhones or iPods, they won't work due to their elongated size.

But my daughter could care less (yes, sarcasm), and for her it's a lot of fun. My gripes come from the paying adult's point of view.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Apptivity Gym for iPhone & iPod Touch Devices

Since there seems to be a few confused, this is a case. Nothing more. Reading the questions asked about this product makes me lose some faith in humanity. I'd love to live in a world where a screen and case cost this little. Oh, and yes you will most likely have to rotate the screen. Not difficult to do and not a flaw in the case. I mean, I guess you could say it's a flaw but how hard is it to type lcd_rotate=2 in a config file?

Buy the screen and mount the pi to it. Then 4 screws gets the pi mounted to the case. Without the back cover there's a decent amount of room for hats, although you may have to clip off the tabs for the cover. I had to do this to make room for an Ice Tower, not a big deal as I never intended to use the cover. This also leaves plenty of room for the camera cable to be routed should you need.

It stays put but for my application the mount angle is a little too shallow. Not a fault of the case as it's mounted only about 2 and a half feet from floor level.

Overall, not bad. I could have printed one but sometimes it's just easier to purchase something. Using for an Octoprint set up near my printer and it's been doing fine.

I'm pleasantly surprised at how good it is- It looks pretty great, and rather than being covered in shiny fingerprint-magnet plastic like most cheap mice, a majority of the surface is textured (almost like a rubberized plastic). The USB receiver fits inside the body of the mouse for storage, which is great for travelling with it as I do. I've owned other mice that did that before too (an old Logitech), but unlike that old Logitech, this one uses a built-in rechargeable battery. To be honest, my Logitech mouse was great but after a couple of years the battery started making a bad connection inside (corroded contacts were keeping the battery from working), so I'd have to try to clean it off every few uses on the road to keep it working. With this product however, it seems less likely that will become a problem. Also, the ability to plug it in and charge it off the computer directly if it starts to die is a great plus!
My first impression was that the mouse was a little jumpier than I expected, but then I noticed the little button under the scroll wheel and discovered that it was for changing the DPI. Honestly, I'm not sure why they put it in such an easy to use spot, I feel like this isn't something that needs to change very often. But a couple of clicks on that button got me to about the mouse speed I like. I'm actually really happy with this product and although I was shopping around for a replacement Logitech, I think I'll keep this one in my travel bag instead!

text_fidelity_a:
Computer Speakers for Desktop/Laptop/Mac, USB Powered PC Speaker, 2.0 Channel Stereo Multimedia Speaker for TV, Notebook, Built-in Diaphragm,3w3w Horn and in-Line Volume Control TOMOT FT-165 There's a lot I really like about these. Let me start off by pointing out, however, these are NOT USB SPEAKERS. They are simply powered off USB and use a standard headphone jack as the audio input. I have to admit, at first I was taken aback by how small they are, and assumed they must produce weak sound as a result (I'm used to a set of Harmon/Kardon speakers on my desktop which are bigger than these). But despite their size, they actually produce a really great and full sound, with an almost exaggerated stereo effect thanks to individual speakers pointing in different directions.
What I love most about it, however, is that it is USB powered. That means no additional plugs needed on my desktop, and in fact they are fantastic for boosting the audio on a laptop. In the included picture I'm posting with this, I have an old Dell Laptop that my kids use to watch things on, and these sound FAR better than the tiny built in laptop speaker. Since it is USB powered, it can be simply be run directly off the laptop itself, no additional wires or outlets necessary. Put one plug into an available USB slot, the other into the headphone jack. It makes a nice and neat looking portable setup. The thing is, I can't help but wonder why it isn't just a 100% USB sound system? I have a pair of headphones that I love using that are completely digital- it identifies as its own sound card when plugged in and requires only that one USB plug. I sort of assumed that this would be something similar to that and therefore require only that ONE plug to operate. In some cases, the digital sound systems are better than analog plug ones (interference, for example) anyway, so it seems strange to have an analog speaker system powered by a digital USB port. But I guess there can be interesting uses for this too.
For example, a device like an older phone with a headphone jack can connect to this which wouldn't work with USB. Or enhancing the speaker of an Echo Dot and powering it off a dual USB outlet (one for the Dot, the other for the speakers). It is definitely an interesting and useful thing to have around! And for the price, color me impressed!
text_fidelity_b: Computer Speakers for Desktop/Laptop/Mac, USB Powered PC Speaker, 2.0 Channel Stereo Multimedia Speaker for TV, Notebook, Built-in Diaphragm,3w3w Horn and in-Line Volume Control TOMOT FT-165

text_fidelity_a:
Vanguard TBH-100 Ball Head (Black) This is my new favorite tripod head. With two controls for setting friction and locking the head in place it's amazingly versatile. The previous ball-head mount I had was either locked or fully loose which made camera control a little scary. With the Vanguard TBH-250 you can have free movement and maintain enough friction to keep your camera from flopping wildly about. You can also lock and unlock the horizontal movement of the head so you can take panoramic shots with ease.

The mount is threaded for 1/4" which is a sleeve that fits inside a 3/8" threaded fitting so the TBH-250 will fit on the majority of tripods on the market. The 3/8" thread fit my Dolica AX620B100 tripod perfectly and even fit, separate from the tripod and with a lot of finagling, in the bag that came with my Dolica tripod. A small tool was included to remove the 1/4" sleeve but a flat head screwdriver would also do the job.

The only thing I'm not crazy about is the camera mount. It's advertized as a 'quick shoe' mount but it's not that quick and if you're not careful it's not that secure. Slightly loosened you can reposition the mount forward and backward about an inch or thereabouts to get better balance. But loosen the camera mount just a slight bit more and the camera will easily pull free of the tripod head. There is a brass pin which keeps the mount from sliding out front to back and that's great but there's no locking or safety latch keeping your camera attached to the tripod.

While we're on the subject of the camera mount the screw holding the mounting plate to the camera requires a screwdriver, coin or in a pinch you can flip the tool for removing the 1/4" thread adapter and tighten the plate to the camera with that. I'm surprised that a tripod head of this quality doesn't include a butterfly nut to hand tighten the plate to the camera.

While I do wish it had a more secure mount and an easier way to attach the shoe to the camera I would still recommend this tripod head. It's very smooth, solidly built and feels like it will last for years.
text_fidelity_b: Vanguard TBH-100 Ball Head (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150)) UPDATE: Six months in, this router has been flawless. AND I've discovered it has its own dynamic DNS support capability. That's a nice feature if you run any sort of server application. So, I continue to be impressed with this product.

---

I will be keeping a close eye on this router, which I just purchased yesterday, because it seems too good to be true. So far, in my 24 hours of usage since purchasing it for $29 at Walmart (sorry, Amazon, I was in a hurry) I have found it to be flexible and powerful in my unusual application, which is remote and requires 100% uptime with occasional bursts of heavy usage. Mine is a factory-fresh rather than refurb unit, incidentally.

I'll admit I had some trouble believing a router this cheap could be as good as this one turned out to be (assuming it stays reliable-- but, the one I bought trumpets a lifetime guarantee on the box). I expected something dumbed-down, with seriously constrained functionality and annoying firmware. (This model's v3 hardware, although Broadcom BCM5356-based, is not compatible with alternative firmware such as DD-WRT due to its problematic NVRAM size.) It's a single-stream design, with an internalized antenna, potentially suggesting performance limitations. And it's from Netgear, which I've frankly not had great luck with before... but it's been years since I've tried one of their products, and the reviews here are generally good. Most of the negative reviews here relate to support experiences, but my networking knowledge-level is expert, so ...what the heck, did I mention it was $29? An easy roll of the dice.

Though my application requires custom configuration, I initially started the unit using its web-based wizard, which you access by connecting your computer (via cable or WiFi) and pointing your browser to 192.168.1.1. With the unit connected to my cable modem, it set itself up quickly and voila, Internet. For most people this would be good enough and the job would be done. Kudos to Netgear for delivering the product with WPA-2 encryption enabled! They provide a SSID and password on a printed label. So, you're good to go. And its default configuration is just fine for most folks' usage.

For my application, however, I needed to cable several devices including a VoIP adaptor (a la [...] and a server with several ports exposed to the Internet. The unit needed to be set to a specific IP address scheme, SSID and password. And a dynamic-DNS utility on the server needed to communicate with my DNS provider. ...To accomplish these and other advanced tasks, the browser-based configurator at 192.168.1.1 has an Advanced tab. Proceeding through the settings is straightforward and similar to other reasonably-configurable routers. The default settings established earlier by the wizard remain intact in the Advanced panes so you are starting from a known-operable configuration. All good.

So I proceeded through each of my customizations, taking care to click the Apply button after modifying any pane. Usually there's a ten-second delay during which the unit sets up the new settings; a few necessitate that the router reboot itself. Everything went smoothly.

So, for $29 I'd replicated an unusual configuration and everything was working. But how well?

Okay so my wife had to take an important international FaceTime call as I was finishing up. So, for a while there the server was downloading some massive updates, two ssh clients were talking to the server, VoIP was in use, six WiFi clients were doing whatever they were doing, a 3G microcell tower was initializing and downloading firmware updates to itself ...and FaceTime was running smoothly with a high frame-rate on her third-gen iPad. A nice acid test!

In particular, I did not feel the need to mess with the unit's default QoS settings... and additional props to Netgear for including QoS in a router this inexpensive!

So far, I'm impressed. It's hard to imagine a better value in a router. I'll update this review if there are any reliability issues, but so far, so good. So excellent, in fact.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150))

We used this bracket to hang our new 75 inch Sony TV. The bracket itself has worked well. We did end up utilizing the extension bracket which gave us added mobility in locating the TV in the center of the wall. Due to our hanging the TV on an interior wall that had a narrow gap between the drywall and cinder block I had to get special wall anchors to support the weight of the TV.

Due to how this bracket is designed it can be difficult to access ports, such as HDMI and USB, once the TV is hung upon the wall.
