3.7V 30W(peak) Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Double Subwoofer Rich Bass, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Speaker Support FM Radio, Small Stereo Sound System for Home, Party, Outdoor Travel(No Light) I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and has several connection methods.

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing ten times (and more) what this does, the sound quality from this speaker is really quite good. In relation to the sound quality I would place them on par with mid to high end Bluetooth speakers.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 2 hours to charge the built in 4000 mAh battery and the speaker lasts a solid 4.5 hours at max volume - 8 hour with volume midway (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings).

There are multiple ways to connect to this speaker including Bluetooth 5.0, which can reach much further than previous versions, through an AUX cable, a 3.5mm jack, TF card, USB flash drive, or FM radio - it even has a built in extendable antenna.

While it has a remote and I tested it and it works fine, I rarely use it as I connect with my phone all the time.

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last couple of months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery, being 4000 mAh, is much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been really good.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: 3.7V 30W(peak) Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Double Subwoofer Rich Bass, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Speaker Support FM Radio, Small Stereo Sound System for Home, Party, Outdoor Travel(No Light)

Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Let me start, we are a family of dedicated logitech-harmony remote users for the over 7 years. We love the easy of set up and allowing you to out in a large number of electrical devices onto one remote.

So we decided to try this one for our bedroom devices and we were somewhat disappointed with the limitations on this model:

1. when using the harmony software there were a lot of limitations when compared with the 900 (and previous models). The limitations included:
a> couldnt change the order of the activities. ie if you want dvd ahead of music, you would not do that. To over come this: you need to preplan the order at which the devices are set up. In the more expensive models and in previous older models, you could set everything up and then re-order them.

b. once you are in a device: it only offers you four functions on the face, instead of 6 to eight. to overcome this you need to scroll to another page.

c. the device has four hard buttons to operate only four devices. Hence this remote is not useful if you have a decent home theatre. okay for a bedroom with a TV, tivo, dvd and music system.

Typical features of the device: all the button light up in the dark, except for the four device buttons and the help button (so you need to learn where they are on the remote). A good thing about this device (we also have the 900) is that the bottom half of the device have a very similar layout so no learning where the volume, channel button are placed.

The software is similar to other harmony remote, but once you indicate which remote you have: the choices are very limited.

It is worth buying the 900 and above for living room devices; and if you could find the 880, its former model, get it as the functionalities are much better. And yes, the software will support this older model. Buy the 700 if it is only for a couple of applicances. However, if you are a harmony user, you will feel a little frustrated with the limitations of this model.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

All-new Fire HD 10 tablet, 10.1", 1080p Full HD, 32 GB, latest model (2021 release), Black, without lockscreen ads The tablet itself is okay; that is, mediocre. It's a sub-hundred dollar Android tablet sans Google Play. Don't compare it to other devices (costing hundreds of dollars more). There was video pixelation as well as motion distortion on YouTube. Then I downloaded 5 Amazon appstore apps. 4 didn't work *at all*. The 5th seemed, again, okay but useless. I used to be a regular Fire user since 2011. I liked most of the tablets and Amazon's appstore through those years. I was APPALLED at the current status. What are the apps for if not Amazon tablets? I don't believe they make phones anymore. It's okay if all you do is watch Amazon video. But you can watch Amazon Prime, listen to Audibles, and read on Kindle on any tablet through their respective apps which work fine. And watch YouTube on a native Android. Why sacrifice?

Note: My Fire HD 10, 7th edition through it's Silk Browser doesn't have these picture and sound problems. Tested same videos on YouTube. Superior picture, no distortion or motion problems, and good sound.

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundLink Bluetooth Speaker III I've had several sets of Bose Companion speakers over the years, but this was my first experience with a Bose Bluetooth product. Setup was quick and easy, and as you can use the speaker as the battery is charging for the first time (plugged in), I had my speaker powered up and connected within five minutes of unpacking. You can pair the SoundLink III with up to six devices and it will automatically connect to the last known device. With a 30-foot range, you can be several rooms away and still get crystal-clear sound.

The sound quality is fantastic...good bass for a speaker this size. You can also REALLY crank up the volume on this one; sound is still full and balanced at max volume. I love that the unit is portable and holds a charge for quite a while (up to 14 hours; the battery lasts up to two years). Because the battery is not user-replaceable, I tend to keep it plugged in when I am using it for long periods.

The one downside is the fact that there is no remote; it would be nice to at least be able to adjust the volume remotely rather than walking over to my phone and using the volume buttons, or walking over to the speaker and using the buttons on top, which are covered with a rubberized layer, but this is a small issue overall.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundLink Bluetooth Speaker III

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers After running out of space for bookcases and space *on* those bookcases, it was suggested that I look into getting an ebook reader. I decided to give a Kindle a try, and it's made the transition from paper to e-ink a mostly painless transition. The Kindle Keyboard is lightweight - even with a cover it's light enough to hold for long periods of time and usually thinner than most books. It's a little bigger than most paperbacks but smaller than hardcovers, to I can fit it into a larger purse and take it with me if I'll have time to kill during any appointments. Of course, it makes traveling much, *much* easier as now I only need to pack the Kindle and one book to read during that 'power off all electrical devices' time.

The 3G version allows more connectivity but does drain the battery faster. If you want to conserve energy, you can turn it off unless you are downloading a book. The keyboard is small, but I haven't found it too tiny to use when unlocking it for use or searching. My only complaint is sometimes trying to remember when to use the 'Menu' button and the 'square' button for some features - it could be a bit more intuitive (like when to remove a book or sample from the device).

The Kindle Keyboard is only 4GB (actually a little less) and can't be expanded beyond that, but it does hold a lot of books. It's also easy to load books by USB cable and sending via email (to Kindle email account). It's definitely saved at least a bookcase or two! While I would hate to see all books go digital, if you do have an issue with space or you want to have a few books always on hand, a Kindle definitely helps in that regard.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

text_fidelity_a: Western Digital 4TB WD Blue PC Internal Hard Drive HDD - 5400 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, 256 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD40EZAZ The price of these is usually low enough to consider buying them new for off-line storage. Something most people don't consider using a hard drive for. 4TB has become small for my purposes, but as off-line storage I don't want to risk more than that on one drive. It's much simpler to archive data on a 4TB hard drive in a dock and keep it in a case than to burn 4TB to a stack of Blu-Ray disks every few months, and DVDs are completely out of the question. I'm archiving around 20TB of 4K video that I've captured with GoPros so far. Most of it is on "retired" drives, but I've run out of reliable older drives and I think I'll be upgrading to these in the future. They're unlikely to store data forever without some degradation, but rewriting the data once a year won't wear them out for decades. These will not work well in an NAS or even a RAID array in a PC, and shouldn't be used in a PC with more than one or two hard drives anyway. They're not designed to cope with vibration from several other drives, but as a single drive or for data backup they're fine. It's a capable drive for typical home use. For full-time use in an array, the Red Plus and Red Pro drives are what I get. If you need to store large amounts of data off-line, or if you just need a new drive in a home PC, this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 4TB WD Blue PC Internal Hard Drive HDD - 5400 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, 256 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD40EZAZ
